data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's causal mechanism never engages the comparative term of the claim: it identifies a shared market signal that can synchronize independent operators, but it provides no causal argument for why this synchronization makes the decentralized network LESS resilient than a single large service with strictly MORE internal redundancy. A large monolith optimizing the same metric via the same rules would synchronize its redundant components through an even tighter coupling (a central scheduler), so the mechanism, as stated, predicts equal vulnerability rather than superior centralized resilience. The target's only comparative countercondition ('if the centralized service also synchronizes... it is equally vulnerable') explicitly yields equality, leaving the stricter comparative claim ('not necessarily more resilient') without a mechanism that distinguishes the two architectures in the direction required.
